title: Implement Datadog Logs intake connector (regional endpoints, API key auth, throttling handling)
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Build the Datadog Logs destination connector for SIEM-ready audit export (beta).

This connector is used by the audit-export worker subsystem to deliver Audit Event v1 records into a customer’s Datadog Logs pipeline.

Key requirements:
- Support Datadog site/region selection (US1/EU1/US3/US5/AP1) and allow an override for Private deployments (custom intake base URL).
- Use API key authentication (no request signing) with least-privilege guidance.
- Correctly handle throttling and transient failures with bounded retries/backoff (avoid retry storms).
- Provide clear error classification and surfaced health signals (last_success_at/last_error + metrics tags by destination + http_status).

Out of scope:
- Customer-specific field mapping beyond our published audit schema.
- Datadog Events API or other Datadog sinks (only Logs intake).
acceptance_criteria:
- Connector can be configured with a `site` (datadoghq.com, datadoghq.eu, us3.datadoghq.com, us5.datadoghq.com, ap1.datadoghq.com) OR `intake_base_url` override (Private).
- Requests authenticate using customer-provided Datadog API key (sent as header). API key is stored via secrets store integration (no plaintext in logs).
- Endpoint selection maps deterministically to the correct Logs intake URL.
- Connector batches events and respects payload size limits (byte-based cap) and request timeouts.
- Retries:
  - 429: retry with exponential backoff + jitter; respect `Retry-After` when present.
  - 5xx / 408 / connection reset / timeout: retry with exponential backoff + jitter.
  - 4xx (except 408/429): treated as non-retryable and transitions destination to degraded with actionable error.
- Emits metrics for request counts, error counts, latency histogram, and bytes sent, tagged by destination_id + sink=datadog + status_code.
- Integration tests exist using a mock HTTP server covering: success, partial failures, 429 with/without Retry-After, 5xx, invalid API key (403), and oversized payload handling.
- Includes docs snippet for recommended Datadog parsing (service/source tags, JSON parsing) and dedupe guidance (at-least-once).
implementation_plan:
1) Config model
- Extend destination schema: `type=datadog` with fields:
  - `site` (enum) OR `intake_base_url` (string; Private override)
  - `api_key_ref` (secret reference)
  - `tags` (optional key/value) for Datadog tags (e.g., env, workspace)
  - `compression` (optional; default gzip enabled)

2) Endpoint mapping
- Default intake path: `/api/v2/logs`.
- Base URL mapping:
  - US1: `https://http-intake.logs.datadoghq.com`
  - EU1: `https://http-intake.logs.datadoghq.eu`
  - US3: `https://http-intake.logs.us3.datadoghq.com`
  - US5: `https://http-intake.logs.us5.datadoghq.com`
  - AP1: `https://http-intake.logs.ap1.datadoghq.com`
- If `intake_base_url` is provided, use it verbatim (validate https scheme unless Private explicitly allows http for in-cluster proxies).

3) Request format
- POST JSON array of events (one per audit event) as Datadog accepts structured logs.
- Headers:
  - `DD-API-KEY: <api_key>`
  - `Content-Type: application/json`
  - `Content-Encoding: gzip` (when enabled)
  - Optional: `User-Agent: redwood-audit-exporter/<version>`

4) Batching constraints
- Cap by bytes (pre-compression) and count to avoid oversized requests.
  - Target: <= 4.5 MiB raw JSON payload and <= 500 events per request.
- If a single event exceeds cap, mark as poison-pill and route to DLQ with reason `event_too_large`.

5) Retry / backoff / circuit-breaker behavior
- Retry budget per destination to prevent cascading backlog growth.
- Exponential backoff with full jitter; base 500ms, max 60s.
- Respect Retry-After seconds when present (bounded to max backoff).
- Classify errors:
  - Retryable: 429, 5xx, 408, network/timeouts.
  - Non-retryable: 400/401/403 (auth), 413 (payload too large -> adjust batching; if persists, degrade), 422 (schema/format), 404 (bad endpoint).
- Integrate with worker’s backpressure controls (pause destination after N consecutive failures / error rate threshold, surface to health endpoint).

6) Observability
- Metrics:
  - `audit_export_sink_requests_total{sink="datadog",destination_id,site,status}`
  - `audit_export_sink_request_latency_ms{...}`
  - `audit_export_sink_bytes_sent_total{...}`
  - `audit_export_sink_events_sent_total{...}`
  - `audit_export_sink_retry_total{reason=...}`
- Logs: do not log API key; include destination_id, tenant/workspace id, correlation id, and Datadog status code.

7) Docs / Supportability
- Provide troubleshooting table (403 invalid key, 429 throttling, 413 payload) and recommended Datadog pipeline parsing.
- Confirm customer-facing messaging: at-least-once delivery; duplicates possible; dedupe via `event.id` + `event.time` (and/or `delivery_id` where present).
risk_notes:
- Throttling is common on customer Datadog orgs; failure to respect Retry-After can create retry storms and backlog amplification.
- Endpoint/site misconfiguration can look like auth failures; validation and clear error messages are important for Support.
- Private deployments may require egress proxying and custom CA bundles; connector should support custom base URL and standard TLS settings (with guardrails).
- Datadog intake returns 202 for accepted logs; do not assume 200-only success.
test_plan:
- Unit tests:
  - Endpoint mapping for each supported `site`.
  - Batch splitting by byte size and count.
  - Error classification matrix (429/5xx/4xx) and retry decision.
  - Redaction tests to ensure API key never appears in logs.

- Integration tests (mock HTTP server):
  - 202 accepted.
  - 429 with Retry-After=2 -> next attempt waits >=2s (bounded by max).
  - 429 without Retry-After -> exponential backoff applies.
  - 500 then 202 -> succeeds and emits success metrics.
  - 403 -> no retry; destination transitions degraded and surfaces actionable error.
  - 413 -> connector reduces batch; if single-event oversize, DLQ.

- Soak test (staging): sustained throughput with synthetic audit events; verify steady-state latency and no uncontrolled retry storms when injecting 429 at 10% rate.
rollout_plan:
- Land behind destination type gate (datadog connector only reachable when feature flag enabled for tenant).
- Enable for 1 internal staging tenant + 1 design partner with Datadog.
- Monitor:
  - sink error rate by status code
  - retry volume
  - backlog depth per destination
  - end-to-end delivery latency
- If 429/5xx triggers backlog growth beyond SLO thresholds, reduce concurrency per destination and/or increase backoff caps per SRE guidance.
